STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a white square plate with a raised rim band and a flat centre, on a glass surface. This is a flat plate (square).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are 20-30 cm. This looks like a medium-sized square dinner plate, so about 25 cm.
b) Reference object: the pizza slices are the only cue. A slice is about 11-12 cm wide at the crust, and the two slices together span roughly 40% of the plate's width across the diagonal. Measured against the slice length (~20 cm tip to crust), the plate side is about 1.3 slice lengths, so roughly 26 cm.
Reconciled width: about 26 cm (square, area ≈ 676 cm²).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Pizza (countable slices): there are two adjacent triangular slices that together form roughly one large slice's worth of area on the plate. Visible: 2 slices, each with a generous wedge. Counting as 2 slices (bread-like pizza slice ~ 1.5 cm thick, but this is a thin crust, so I use ~80 g per slice as a standard wedge; the crust is thicker at the edge).
  - Footprint: the two slices cover about 22% of the plate area ≈ 149 cm².
  - Average thickness: crust rim ~1.5 cm, cheese/sauce centre ~0.8 cm, average ≈ 1.2 cm.
  - Volume ≈ 149 × 1.2 ≈ 179 ml; pizza bulk density ~0.6 g/ml (bread-like with air) → ≈ 107 g.
  - Cross-check: 2 slices × 30-40 g each for a thin slice is too low given the thick crust; using the countable method, 2 slices × ~55 g ≈ 110 g. Consistent with the footprint estimate.
- Tomato sauce: thin smear under cheese, mostly included in the pizza mass above.
- Mozzarella cheese: visible melted on top, roughly 20% of the pizza mass, already counted in the total.

Pizza total ≈ 110 g. The food is flat, one layer; no hidden base layer beyond the crust.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: none beyond the slices themselves; a few pieces on a large plate stay light.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g: Cheese pizza (cooked, Margherita-style, served) ≈ 260 kcal/100 g.
Energy ≈ 110 × 2.6 ≈ 286 kcal.
